proof_checks.minimum: The proof establishes that any 4-regular graph on 25 vertices with at most 12 changed views must retain at least one untouched edge, because 12 vertices can touch at most 48 of the 50 edges. This untouched edge bounds the candidate minimum both above and below by the original minimum μ, forcing the minimum to remain exactly μ=1984. This holds for the source event and two further deletions (at most 3 changed views). To raise the minimum, all 50 original edges must be covered by changed views. Since the maximum independent set of the 5x5 grid (five disjoint 5-cycles) is 10, at most 10 views can remain untouched. Thus, at least 15 views must change, meaning at least 14 distinct views besides the source A must prune to allow a higher minimum.
proof_checks.fixture: At state S_1 (after A deletes T), the work entries for A and B against all other views become identical, because deleting T (subtotal 2, square 4) adds 4 to W_{Aj} for j in D=N(A) and subtracts 4 for j in E=N(B), matching B's original entries. The A-B work drops from μ+14 to μ+10. In the minimum graph, A loses its 4 edges to D and gains 4 edges to E. Consequently, labels in D drop to degree 3, labels in E rise to degree 5, and all others remain degree 4. All off-diagonal excesses above μ are restricted to {0,4,8,10,12,20,24}. The fixture dictates that T, U, R are the only subtotal-2 features. A holds R's exclusive child, preventing A from deleting R without violating the non-leaf rule, and A never holds U. Furthermore, for any i in E and j in D, the excess cannot be 4, because an excess of 4 requires an opposite pair sharing a center whose perpendicular pair contains A or B, which would imply i or j shares a neighbor with A or B in their independent neighbor sets, an impossibility.
proof_checks.same_view: If a single view i not in {A,B} makes two deletions, it must remove exactly one minimum edge from each of the four labels in E to reduce their degrees from 5 to 4. Since no other edges can change, i must be adjacent to all unedited labels in E. If i is in E, it cannot be adjacent to the rest of E because E is an independent set. If i is not in E, it cannot be adjacent to both 11 and 13 (opposite horizontal members of E) because they only share B as a common neighbor. Thus, no single editor outside A,B can fix E. If the sole editor is A or B, it must supply an edge to every label in D (currently at μ+4). This requires the two deletions to change the work by exactly -4. However, the sum or difference of two positive integer squares can never equal 4 (since s_1^2 + s_2^2 = 4 has no positive integer solution, and m^2 - n^2 = 4 implies (m-n)(m+n)=4 which has no solution for m>n>0). This rules out any single-editor depth-two recovery.
proof_checks.different_views: For two deletions in different views, both must have even subtotals; an odd subtotal would make the editor's work against all untouched views odd, leaving it with at most one minimum edge (to the other editor) and failing the degree-four requirement. At least two labels in D remain untouched and need one added minimum edge from an editor. This requires an excess of exactly the deleted feature's square. The only available even square is 4 (subtotal 2). Deleting T increases work against D, so it cannot be T. E has no excess 4 against D, and A cannot delete R, leaving (B,U) as the only possible deletion that can supply the edge. Thus, one of the edits must be (B,U). Comparing the proposed two-edit path to the established one-edit recovery (B,U), the second editor i must maintain the same edges to untouched views to satisfy 4-regularity. However, its deletion changes all its off-diagonal work entries by a nonzero square, destroying its original minimum edges and contradicting 4-regularity.
proof_checks.scope: The proof successfully deduces that there are zero depth-two recoveries for both the primary fixed-minimum gate G and the diagnostic degree-only gate G'. It analytically confirms the preregistered enumeration's BRANCH ONE: the only recovering first actor within K=2 is B=12, the only move is (12,2), and it occurs at depth one, with no depth-two completions. Consequently, any recovery avoiding view 12 requires at least three further deletions and more than one further editor. The proof explicitly limits its claims to the retained-tree model and the supplied geometry gate, leaving physical recovery enforcement, receiver access, scheduling, and gravity correspondence strictly open, matching the preregistered claim limits.
